newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble slips on new T-bill tax, inflation rate.
newsitem.headline: Rouble slips on new T-bill tax, inflation rate.

text.p: The rouble slipped on Wednesday as some banks transferred funds into dollars following a new tax on government securities and a fall in Treasury bill yields, dealers said.
rouble/dollar Feb 5 midday Feb 5 early Feb 4 close
"The rouble has been slipping smoothly since the very beginning of the day," a dealer said, adding there was strong client demand for dollars.

Dealers said that a new 15 percent tax on earnings from government securities, finally cleared by the Justice Ministry on Tuesday, and falling yields on T-bills made some banks withdraw their funds from bills and bonds.
"T-bill yields are falling and some banks are transferring their money into shares, some into dollars," said Andrei Trebumskikh, chief dealer at United Investment Bank.
He also said the rouble was adjusting for inflation, which quickened to 2.3 percent in January, while the rouble had depreciated by 1.3 percent.
